mappings.note: Garibaldi's nationality: a named unifier of Italy, so the nation-state-formation outcome LO-3 and not LO-2 (no movement or ism is in play); the demand is bare retrieval, hence C-1.1 rather than leaving LO-3 to imply analysis
matches Cavour/Mazzini/Garibaldi/Victor Emmanuel to their roles in making Italy; Mazzini appears here as a unifier, not as the founder of a secret society, so LO-3 not LO-2. Matching = C-1.1
chronology of Greece, Italy and Germany becoming states; three of the four events are nation-formation, so majority rule sends it to LO-3 and Napoleon's defeat does not pull in LO-1

Young Europe is a revolutionary secret society, i.e. one of the 'diverse social movements of the time' (LO-2); no state is being formed here, which is what separates it from the Mazzini-as-unifier items on LO-3

reads the upper register of Sorrieu's 1848 print; the content is the vision of a Europe of nation states (LO-3), and because the frame has no visual-source outcome the stimulus-reading demand is carried by C-1.2

Balkans as the post-1871 flashpoint and Ottoman decline as its cause: the road-to-war outcome. Assertion-reason judging whether R explains A is itself the causal evaluation LO-4 names, so no competency is added
Byron is the romantic poet mobilising west European sympathy, so the cultural-movement outcome LO-2; the Greek state itself (treaty, independence) is what goes to LO-3. Identification = C-1.1
Act of Union 1707 forming Great Britain is nation-state formation without revolution, LO-3; nothing about the French Revolution is asked so LO-1 stays out

an even chronological split: 1789 and Napoleon's 1815 defeat are LO-1, Sorrieu 1848 and Victor Emmanuel 1861 are LO-3, and a student who knows only one half cannot order the list, so both content codes are genuine

the imperial world map is nationalism in its post-1871 narrow phase, still LO-3 ('in Europe and elsewhere'); a supplied image read for its meaning takes C-1.2 as the nearest legal hook for source work
Denmark, Austria and France as Prussia's three wars: the mechanics of German state-making, LO-3, recalled rather than analysed

Congress of Vienna and Metternich belong to conservatism, the ism that sits beside liberalism and romanticism in LO-2's 'diverse social movements'; LO-1 is reserved for France's own action, not for the settlement that reversed it

Rebmann's Jacobin almanac cover is French revolutionary imagery reaching the German states, LO-1; the picture is only a prompt for a remembered name, so C-1.1 and not the C-1.2 used for genuine image-reading
three factual statements about the Balkans to be sifted, not a cause to be weighed; same LO-4 content as the assertion-reason item above but C-1.1 marks the lower demand

Greek independence 1821 as a nation emerging from the Ottoman Empire, LO-3 rather than LO-2, because the subject is the state won and not the sympathy that supported it; causal assertion-reason needs no added competency
the Silesian weavers of 1845 are the social-distress strand of LO-2; the cause is retrieved from the text rather than argued, so C-1.1
Marianne and Germania give the abstract nation a concrete form, which is the idea-of-nationalism content of LO-3; no image is supplied and the task is naming, so C-1.1 not C-1.2
Treaty of Constantinople 1832 is Greece becoming a state, the LO-3 side of the Greek material; a treaty name is pure recall
the caricature of Napoleon's retreat must actually be read to know the sheets are lost territories; content is Napoleonic France (LO-1) and the image-reading demand takes C-1.2
the Civil Code of 1804 is the concrete instrument by which revolutionary France changed Europe, LO-1; the item asks which provision is absent, i.e. recall of the code's contents

the Zollverein is an institution built towards German unity, so it goes to LO-3 under the rule that isms go to LO-2 and nation-building institutions to LO-3, even though the concept tag reads 'Liberal nationalism'

the whole point is that Britain's slow state-making (LO-3) and the French Revolution as nationalism's first expression (LO-1) are true but unrelated; the item cannot be answered from either outcome alone, so both are cited and neither is decorative
Mazzini and Victor Emmanuel II in the Italian unification table; the same unifier-versus-secret-society split as above puts this on LO-3
naming liberalism as the ideology of free markets is an ism as an idea, which is LO-2 territory; contrast the Zollverein item, where the same theme appears as an institution and goes to LO-3
all four events are Napoleon's own career, so unlike the mixed chronology item this one sits wholly on LO-1; ordering dates is C-1.1
